en.name: Shacha sauce
en.summary: Shacha is a savoury paste of dried shrimp, brill fish, garlic, shallot and spices suspended in oil — the hotpot and stir-fry staple sold in tins and jars. Unopened it keeps about 18–24 months in the cupboard. Once opened, refrigerate it and use within about 3–6 months.
en.pantry: Unopened tins and jars keep on the shelf to the printed date, about 18–24 months from purchase, in a cool dry cupboard. The paste separates and a layer of oil sits on top; that is normal and is part of how the jar is preserved. Salt and low water activity are barriers to pathogen growth in their own right, which is why a sealed commercial jar needs no refrigeration. Do not keep a tin that is bulging, rusted or leaking.
en.fridge: Refrigerate after opening at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use within about 3–6 months — a figure borrowed from oyster sauce, the closest salted Chinese seafood-based sauce with a published number. Keep the oil layer covering the paste: that seal is what keeps the dried shrimp and fish in it from going rancid. Use a clean dry spoon and smooth the surface flat again afterwards. The oil sets solid in the cold, so stand the jar out for a few minutes before scooping. Homemade shacha, fried fresh from shallot, garlic and dried seafood and not shelf-stabilised, is a different product and should be treated as a fresh aromatic oil.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for shacha sauce and no need for one: it is salty and oily enough to keep for months in the fridge, which is longer than most households take to finish a jar. Freezing a high-oil paste also achieves little, since it will not set hard and the texture coarsens. If you have a large tin, decant it into two smaller jars so the one in use is opened less often.
spoilage: A rancid, crayon-like or fishy-off smell from the oil or the dried seafood
Mould on the surface or on paste standing above the oil
A bulging tin, a domed lid, or fizzing on opening
The paste dried into a hard dark crust around the rim
tips: Always level the surface and let the oil settle back over the paste.
Use a clean dry spoon; water is what starts mould in a salty paste.
Stand the jar out for a few minutes before scooping — the oil sets in the fridge.
Decant a large tin into two smaller jars so one stays sealed.

faq.q: Does shacha sauce need to be refrigerated after opening?
faq.a: Yes. Refrigerate at 4 °C or below and use within about 3–6 months, keeping the oil layer over the paste.

faq.q: How long does an unopened tin of shacha keep?
faq.a: About 18–24 months from purchase in a cool dry cupboard, to the printed date.

faq.q: Why is there a layer of oil on top?
faq.a: The paste separates naturally, and that oil layer is part of how the jar keeps — it seals the dried seafood from air. Smooth the surface so it settles back.
There is no timeline and no need. It keeps for months refrigerated, and freezing coarsens the texture.

zh.name: 沙茶醬
zh.summary: 沙茶醬是把蝦米、扁魚、蒜頭、紅蔥和香料炒製後懸浮在油裡的鹹香醬，是火鍋和快炒的必備品，以罐頭和玻璃罐販售。未開封放櫥櫃大約 18～24 個月。開封後請冷藏，並在大約 3～6 個月內用完。
zh.pantry: 未開封的罐頭和玻璃罐放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃，到標示日期為止，從購買日起算大約 18～24 個月。醬體會分離、上面浮一層油，這是正常的，也是這罐能夠保存的一部分。鹽和低水活性本身就是抑制病原菌的屏障，這就是未開封的市售罐不需要冷藏的原因。罐身鼓起、生鏽或滲漏的就不要留。
zh.fridge: 開封後請放 4 °C 以下冷藏，並在大約 3～6 個月內用完——這個數字借自蠔油，那是資料中最接近的中式鹹味海鮮基底醬且有公布數字。請讓油層始終蓋住醬體：那層封面正是防止裡面的蝦米和扁魚走油耗的東西。用乾淨乾燥的湯匙，取完把表面抹平。低溫下油會凝固，挖之前把罐子放著回溫幾分鐘。自製沙茶是用新鮮紅蔥、蒜頭和乾貨現炒、沒有做常溫穩定處理的產品，屬於另一回事，應該當成新鮮香料油看待。
zh.freezer: 沙茶醬沒有冷凍期限，也不需要：它夠鹹、油又多，冷藏就能放好幾個月，比多數家庭用完一罐的時間還長。冷凍一罐高油脂的醬效果也有限，它不會真的凍硬，質地反而變粗。一大罐的話，建議分裝成兩小罐，正在用的那罐才不會被反覆開闔。
spoilage: 油或乾貨發出油耗味、蠟筆味或不對勁的腥味
醬面或露出油面的醬體長霉
罐身鼓起、蓋子鼓起，或開罐時冒氣
罐口周圍的醬乾成深色硬殼
tips: 每次取完都把表面抹平，讓油回到醬體上方。
用乾淨乾燥的湯匙；鹹醬長霉的起點就是水。
挖之前先把罐子放幾分鐘——冷藏時油會凝固。
大罐分裝成兩小罐，其中一罐保持密封。

faq.a: 要。放 4 °C 以下冷藏，並在大約 3～6 個月內用完，過程中讓油層蓋住醬體。

faq.q: 未開封的沙茶醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃，從購買日起算大約 18～24 個月，以標示日期為準。

faq.q: 上面那層油是怎麼回事？
faq.a: 醬體本來就會分離，而那層油是它得以保存的一部分——它把乾貨和空氣隔開。取用後把表面抹平，讓油回到上面。
沒有對應期限，也沒有必要。它冷藏就能放好幾個月，冷凍反而會讓質地變粗。
